Q116276234.summary: Set in a gold-leaf roundel on dark glass, the youthful Christ stands at the top holding out a wreath in each hand over the heads of Saints Peter and Paul, who sit facing one another below; an inscription runs around the border. Once the base of a drinking bowl, it celebrates the two great apostles of Rome receiving from Christ the crown of martyrdom.
facts: Gold-glass bowl bases like this survived in large numbers because they were pressed into the mortar of catacomb graves as markers; mortar still clings to this one.
Peter and Paul, martyred in Rome, were the most popular saints on Roman gold glass of the 4th century.
Q116276234.notes: The worklist's 'c' (place made) field was correct; set repeats Met culture/place for clarity. The inscription is not transcribed here because it was not verified letter by letter.
